strongest_case_against_the_verdict: Frame the quantity as the in-sample ROC AUC of a plasma-exosomal non-coding-RNA signature for MCI against community controls in Chinese elderly, measured by ultracentrifugation and qPCR. Task (T1), modality family (fluid, plasma exosomal RNA) and validation tier (both contested AUCs are in-sample) then match, the metric type is the same, and the one failing gate (dataset family: Guangzhou v Gansu community cohorts) is of the kind the review once waived (C-232, ADNI v NACC). Each study's uncertainty excludes the other's estimate: P-1232's 0.641-0.760 excludes 0.901, and a Hanley-McNeil interval for 0.901 with 24 v 24 (about 0.81-0.99, reader's calculation) excludes 0.700. Two ordering-type statements could be read as crossing the pair: P-1232 says its combination was 'more credible' than single markers and that exosomal lncRNAs 'may offer a broader research space and prospect ... compared to miRNAs', while a single exosomal miRNA in P-1254 beats the lncRNA panel by 0.20. A second shared quantity also seems to split: P-1254 finds education and regular exercise significantly associated with MCI and concludes that they 'help older people maintain cognitive function', whereas P-1232 finds no case-control difference in education or physical activity.
why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: It does not succeed. (1) 'A plasma-exosomal ncRNA signature' is not one estimand: an AUC belongs to a specific predictor in a specific population, the rule names predictor set as a quantity difference, and it lists 'two different methods each reporting a different score where neither study claims the ordering the other refutes' as not incompatible. Neither paper measures the other's markers. In summaries.md, miR-483-5p, miR-502-5p and the three lncRNAs occur only in these two blocks, and the other exosomal-miRNA papers (e.g. P-1323) use different miRNAs, so there is no same-marker or bridging study. (2) The ordering-type statements stay inside one paper: 'more credible' compares the panel with its own three lncRNAs; the lncRNA-versus-miRNA sentence is hedged ('may'), concerns research scope, and is derived from 'a broader range of biological functions', not from accuracy data (P-1232 measured no miRNA); P-1254 never mentions lncRNAs. (3) Waiving the dataset family would not help: the C-232 cohort waiver was later judged insufficient because predictor-set and horizon differences remained, and here predictor set, case definition (education-specific MMSE v uncorrected MoCA < 26) and control group all differ. The control groups are age/sex-matched v 4.8 years younger, and P-1254 prints a MoCA SD of 1.14 around 26.17, which 24 integer scores all at or above 26 cannot produce. (4) The lifestyle quantities fail Section 5.2: education is same-direction (illiterate 10.3% v 7.1% of cases v controls in P-1232; 20/99 v 3/176 in P-1254) with a significance-only difference. The exercise contrast sets a null with no supported direction (88.4% v 87.1% regular, p = 0.729, age/sex-matched) against a crude association in a sample whose MCI cases average 78.17 v 71.21 years. Neither paper reports an interval, and the dataset-family gate fails for these quantities too. (5) The performance-validity flag is correctly not applied to P-1254 (AUC 0.901; accuracy 43/48 = 0.896 at the reported operating point), consistent with its application to P-988 (AUC 1.0) in C-236; applying it would only add a further bar to genuine. (6) I also tested the other direction, false_positive: the record uses the 'Both findings (can) stand' fork template that the first reader labelled false_positive in C-235 and C-236. There, the claimed opposition dissolved on reading (misread papers, same-direction results). Here a non-overlapping numeric gap survives and the record keeps open that it is an artefact, so the precise failure is the quantity (outcome 2). The first reader's verdict and grounds stand.
grounds: The two AUCs are for different predictors, a logistic combination of three exosomal lncRNAs in P-1232 and one literature-preselected exosomal miRNA in P-1254, and neither study measures the other's markers, so under the rule (predictor set) they are different quantities [e1, e10, e17].

The only ordering-type statements stay inside one paper: P-1232's 'more credible' compares its panel with its own three lncRNAs, and its lncRNA-versus-miRNA sentence is a hedged remark about research scope derived from breadth of biological function, not an accuracy result (P-1232 measured no miRNA), while P-1254 never mentions lncRNAs [e2, e3, e4].

The populations behind the shared 'MCI vs healthy controls' label differ: education-specific MMSE cut-offs with age/sex-matched controls against MoCA < 26 with controls 4.8 years younger than the cases, on two scales for which neither paper reports a common metric [e5, e6, e12, e16].

P-1254's age-matched controls cannot all be normal by its own MoCA >= 26 rule unless its table is misprinted, because 24 integer scores all at or above 26 with mean 26.17 allow a standard deviation of at most about 0.82, not the printed 1.14 (reader's arithmetic) [e12, e16].

The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver on record, and a waiver would not change the outcome: C-232's cohort waiver was itself judged insufficient once predictor-set differences were found, and the predictor sets differ here too.

The numeric gap is real in form (P-1232's interval 0.641-0.760 excludes 0.901; a Hanley-McNeil interval of about 0.81-0.99 for 0.901 with 24 v 24, reader's calculation, excludes 0.700), so the verdict rests on the quantity difference and not on noise [e1, e10].

The second quantity both papers report, lifestyle correlates of MCI, gives no contradiction under Section 5.2: education points the same way in both with a significance-only difference, and for exercise P-1232's age/sex-matched null (p = 0.729) has no direction of its own while P-1254's crude association (p = 0.017) comes from a sample whose cases are about 7 years older, with no interval reported by either [e7, e8, e11, e13, e14, e15].

The performance-validity flag correctly does not apply to P-1254 (highest AUC 0.901; implied accuracy 43/48 = 0.896), consistent with the first reader's use of the 0.97 threshold for P-988 (AUC 1.0, C-236), so it neither blocks nor supports genuine here [e10].

The architectural-fork alternative (false_positive) was tested because the record shares the 'Both findings (can) stand' template of C-235 and C-236, but here a non-overlapping numeric gap survives the reading and the record keeps open that it is artefact, so documented_incommensurability is the precise outcome; both labels exclude genuine.

corrections_to_first_reader: No factual error found; all 16 of the first reader's quotes were found verbatim on the stated pages, and its numbers (0.700 and 0.641-0.760; 0.901 and 0.872; 24 v 24 ROC; 43/48 = 0.896; Hanley-McNeil about 0.81-0.99; 4.8-year age gap) check against the PDFs.

Minor refinement to record_defects (claim_a 'n=310 discovery'): Results 3.1 says 10 MCI patients and their controls were sequenced 'and another 300 samples' went to qRT-PCR, out of 310; that arithmetic implies ten sequenced samples in total, so the passage need not conflict with Methods 2.2's five pairs.

Addition, not a correction: the first reader did not test the lifestyle quantities (education, exercise) that both papers report, or the P-1254 control-group MoCA distribution; both were checked here and neither changes the outcome.
